name: BORTEZOMIB
approved_for: Neoplasms
proposed_repositioned_use: Tumour-directed: proteasome inhibition to exploit the proteotoxic stress of aneuploid cells, if the child develops a tumour (rhabdomyosarcoma or Wilms tumour are the tumours reported in this syndrome). It does not treat the constitutional defect.
caveat: The support is from yeast and cancer cells and no paper on proteasome inhibitors in BUB1B-deficient cells was verified. In cell lines there is no association with checkpoint strength before adjusting; after adjusting for proliferation the direction is the same as for microtubule agents (less effective with a weak checkpoint). The network proximity of this class is membership of the proteasome in the checkpoint pathways, so it is not independent evidence.
how_to_validate_or_refute: Dose-response of a proteasome inhibitor in patient-derived cells or BUB1B-hypomorphic engineered cells against isogenic controls; read-outs: selective killing of aneuploid cells (karyotype or single-cell sequencing) and proteotoxic stress markers (ubiquitinated proteins, HSP70). Refuted if aneuploid and diploid cells are equally sensitive.
acts_on: inhibits ADRM1 (curated mechanism); inhibits PSMA1 (curated mechanism); inhibits PSMA2 (curated mechanism)
justification: Satisfies L1 robust proximity, L2 binding to a module protein, L3 literature rationale; does not satisfy none; PRISM: no association with checkpoint strength. Its proximity comes only from membership of generic complexes (proteasome or tubulin): it disappears when they are removed from the modules. Broad target profile: closeness may reflect breadth.
